items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 30:1
items.html: Since the Daat that couples the Hochma and Bina of Arich Anpin at the time of the ascent is the aspect of the Mazal, because its Tifferet is not sufficient, as in Answer 28 above, it follows that at the time of the descent of Arich Anpin to its place, when the Mazal again becomes the aspect of the surrounding lights, the aspect of the screen fit for that coupling is missing. Hence the Daat has no aspect of coupling in the head, and this stature that came out at the time of the ascent descends to the aspect of VAK, which stands at the back of the Tifferet. For the face of the Tifferet is the aspect of the first three of Bina, where Aba and Ima are clothed in the stature of SAG, as is known; therefore the Daat is discerned as the backside of the Tifferet, which is called the shoulders. As in Answer 28 above, see there. (Page 303, Items 15-16; and Page 390, Item 193).
